Preliminary version for the project team. The data come from the 2017 Agricultural Census (IBGE), INCRA/SIPRA (as at 3 June 2025), SEEG 13 (1970–2024) and the 2006 and 2017 Agricultural Censuses. Each value is shown with its reference year. English translation under review. If the two versions differ, the Portuguese text prevails.

Amazon T2 · Tenure awaiting title, unspecialised provisional label IBGE code 5107750

Amazon 80.4% · Cerrado 19.6% of the territory (IBGE, Biomes 1:250,000, 2019). The municipality is grouped by its dominant biome.

RESA Project Manuscript 1 assigns the municipality to type T2, a group of 25 municipalities, in its municipal typology of family farming. The typology applies k-means, with k = 5, to scores from a factor analysis of 21 variables in the 2017 Agricultural Census. Typology details.

The 2017 Agricultural Census of the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) recorded 436 family farms in Salto do Céu, or 72.9% of the municipality’s agricultural establishments (68.8% for Mato Grosso as a whole). They occupied 24,041 ha, or 16.5% of the area of agricultural establishments, averaging 55.1 ha per establishment (municipal median in the Amazon biome: 69.8 ha; Mato Grosso mean: 62.9 ha). Persons employed on family farms totalled 922. The value of family-farm production was R$21.5 million (2017 values), equivalent to R$49.3 thousand per establishment. Animal production accounted for 98.0% of this value.

In 2017, 6.7% of family farms had a tractor, 12.6% received technical guidance and 18.6% obtained financing (municipal medians in the Amazon biome: 16.6%, 12.6% and 17.7%). In addition, 55.0% of family farms produced mainly for their own consumption and 58.9% produced cow’s milk.

On land tenure, the 2017 Census recorded 59 family farms in category 46504 (status of grantee or settler awaiting a definitive title), or 13.5% of the municipality’s family farms (10.8% for Mato Grosso as a whole). The Agrarian Reform Projects Information System (SIPRA) of the National Institute for Colonisation and Agrarian Reform (INCRA) records 2 settlement projects based in the municipality, with 73 settled families and 1,336 ha (Report 0227, as at 3 June 2025). Each project is counted only in its host municipality. Category 46504 understates the extent of agrarian reform, because producers who have already obtained their title appear as owners. See Census tenure data and agrarian reform for a discussion.

For 2024, the Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Removals Estimation System (SEEG 13) estimated gross emissions of 591.6 thousand tCO2e (GWP-AR5) for the whole municipality, not only for family farming. Of this total, 29.4% came from land-use change and forestry and 69.8% from agriculture and livestock. Removals in the same year totalled 133.4 thousand tCO2e. Between the 2006 and 2017 Agricultural Censuses, the number of agricultural establishments in the municipality (family and non-family farms) rose by 37.5%, and their area rose by 69.0%.
